derivation: git log --diff-filter=A -1 -- <every input of the replay>: the newest commit that added any of them. A replay needs a tree holding ALL its inputs, so the pin is the max, and each add-commit is AT OR AFTER the run that produced that input.
note: Re-checking runs the declared revision against these manifests UNCHANGED. The manifests are the blind author's output and are never edited to suit a later tool.

replays.name: extract-A
replays.blocked: The frame and branch registries were built by out-of-band `add-frame` / `add-branch` calls that no tracked file records. A-facts.json carries no `frames` and no `branches` key, yet its facts cite 4 frames (ground, hale, junia, pike) and 4 non-main branches (burn, confront, quiet, reveal), so the first fact fails with `frame 'ground' not present`. Reconstructing the registrations would be AUTHORING a step, not replaying one — the descriptions are lost — so this replay stays blocked until the registrations are recorded, and is never repaired by editing the manifests.

replays.name: extract-B
replays.blocked: Same as extract-A: B-facts.json carries no `frames` and no `branches` key while its facts cite 4 frames (ground, hale, junia, pike) and 5 non-main branches (burn, confront, quiet, reveal_confront, reveal_quiet), and the registrations that created them were never recorded.

step_note: The order is derived from the ids, not from the runbook's prose: the `-facts-add` fact is disjoint from `-facts` and is the target of one typing proposal and one succession edge, so it must land after the base facts and before both proposal imports. B-facts-payoff.json (2 facts) is referenced by no proposal, so its position is unconstrained by the record; it is placed with the other fact imports. When this replay is unblocked, a wrong order fails loudly rather than silently.
